Source A says visitor numbers to the old quarter doubled in five years and forty new businesses opened and 600 jobs were created. Source B says my rent tripled and the tailor and the coffee shop beside me have gone and a souvenir shop and a bar took their place.

they are different about weather tourism is good for the shops there. A say 'forty new businesses opened' which mean business is doing well. but B say 'the tailor and the coffee shop beside me have gone' so the old shops is closing down, not doing well.

They are similar that new shops came, A count 'forty new businesses' and B name 'a souvenir shop and a bar'. Also the purpose is not the same. A is the tourism board own report so it want to show its work is a success, thats why it only count jobs and visitors. B is talking to a heritage society and want people to feel sad about what is lost, so he say 'the old quarter is leaving'.
It is useful because it is a blog by someone who actually went to the old quarter and it talks about the shophouses and street art, so it is about heritage.

I think tourism is good for heritage because when tourists come the government will spend money to keep the old buildings nice. In my opinion we should preserve heritage because it is our roots and young people nowadays dont care. So the source is useful to me.

It is useful as it show that tourism has kept the old buildings. The blogger say 'the shophouses are beautifully restored' so the buildings are looked after and not torn down, which mean the heritage is preserve.

It is useful as it show that tourism has kept the old buildings. The blogger say 'the shophouses are beautifully restored' so the buildings are looked after. But it is limited also. The blogger only 'spent a whole day' there, so it dont tell us anything about the people who live and work there or whether the old trades are still around, and heritage is not just buildings.

It is useful because it show the buildings are kept, 'the shophouses are beautifully restored'. But it is limited, the blogger was only there for one day and only see how it look. When I check with Source B, the shop owner say 'the tailor and the coffee shop beside me have gone'. So the buildings are there but the old way of life is going and C cannot see that. So C is only useful for how the quarter look, not useful for whether the real heritage is preserved.

I agree. Tourism bring in a lot of money for the country and when I went overseas the old towns were all full of tourists and the shops were doing very well. Without tourist the place will be very quiet and boring. So tourism has been good.
Source A and Source D agree with the statement. Source B disagree with the statement. Source C also agree. So three sources agree and only one disagree, therefore I agree to a large extent.

I agree. Source A say '600 jobs were created' so people in the old quarter have work because of the tourists. Source D also agree, the tour guide say without tourists the shophouses 'would have been pulled down years ago', so tourism save the buildings.

Source A agree because '600 jobs were created' so people have work. Source D agree, without tourists the shophouses 'would have been pulled down years ago'. However Source B disagree. The shop owner say 'my rent tripled' so the old shops cannot afford to stay. In conclusion some sources agree and some sources disagree, so tourism is good in some ways and bad in other ways.

Source A agree because '600 jobs were created'. Source D agree, without tourists the shophouses 'would have been pulled down years ago'. Source B disagree, he say 'my rent tripled' and the old shops 'have gone'. I trust A less because it is the tourism board and it look good when the numbers are good, it never say who lost out. B and D both live there so they know, and actually both can be true, tourism saved the buildings but push out the old shops. So I agree only to some extent, good for buildings and jobs but not for the old community.
Source C tells me that most complaints the town council receive are about a few owners who let their cats roam and that they cannot inspect every flat.
Cats are cute but some people are allergic to them. I think people should be allowed to keep cats because dogs are already allowed in flats. Source C is from a town council officer in a newspaper.
It tells me the problem is not really the cats, it is the owners who are irresponsible.
The problem is cause by a few careless owners and not by all cats. This is because the officer says 'we cannot inspect every flat'.

the problem is from a small number of owner and not from all the cats. the officer say most complaint are about 'a few owners who let their cats roam'. this show its the roaming that make the trouble, and roaming is something the owner can stop, so most cat owner are not the problem.
It is not reliable because it is by a cat welfare group so of course they will say cats are good. It is biased.
It is reliable because it gives numbers. It says '120 cats were registered, sterilised and kept indoors' and complaints 'fell from 31 a year to 9', so cats can be kept responsibly in flats.

I think Source B is reliable. Firstly it has a lot of facts and figures. It says '120 cats were registered, sterilised and kept indoors'. That is a lot of cats. Secondly it says the complaints 'fell from 31 a year to 9', which is a big drop. A source with so many numbers is not just an opinion. Therefore it is reliable, cats can be kept responsibly and the numbers prove it. That is why I say it is reliable.

It is quite reliable. B say when the cats were 'kept indoors' the complaints 'fell from 31 a year to 9'. I check with Source C and the officer say most complaints are about owners 'who let their cats roam'. So C agree with B, if the cat stay inside the main problem is gone.

It is quite reliable but not fully. B say when cats were 'kept indoors' complaints 'fell from 31 a year to 9', and Source C support it because the officer say most complaints are about owners 'who let their cats roam'. But B is a fact sheet by a group that 'wants the rule changed', and it is only a pilot in 'one estate' with owners who chose to register their cat. It is written to persuade the ministry and the public, so they pick the good result. So I trust the numbers but not that every owner will be so responsible.

It is saying that cat owners have to hide their cats for too long already. The cat is stuck behind a window and the caption say '34 years in hiding'.

It is saying that cat owners have to hide their cats for too long already. The cat is stuck behind a window and the caption say '34 years in hiding'. It is for the public to see, especially people who own cats or like cats, because it is an online poster that anyone can share.

It say cat owners had to hide their cats for too long, the caption is '34 years in hiding' and the cat is stuck behind a window. The group want people to write to the ministry to change the rule, that is why it say 'Tell the ministry it's time'.

The poster say cat owners been hiding their cats too long, the cat is behind a window and it say '34 years in hiding'. It is for the public, mostly cat owners and people who pity them. It came out on the same day the ministry opened the consultation and it give the date 'Consultation closes 30 June'. So the group want these people to quickly write in to the ministry to support changing the rule before the consultation close.
They are similar because both Source A and Source D are from people in the technology industry. A is a chief executive and D is an engineer. Both are about hiring foreigners.

Source A says we hired 40 engineers from abroad because we could not find these skills here and their projects created 150 more jobs. Source D says I learnt cloud systems from a colleague from abroad who sat next to me for two years and I now lead a team of twelve.

they are similar because both show foreigners is good for the locals. A say their projects 'created 150 more jobs, most of them filled by locals'. D say he learnt from 'a colleague from abroad' and now he 'lead a team of twelve', so the local worker also gain.

they are similar because both show foreigners is good for the locals. A say their projects 'created 150 more jobs, most of them filled by locals'. D say he learnt from 'a colleague from abroad' and now he 'lead a team of twelve'. But they are different in what the benefit is. A is about how many jobs, '150 more jobs'. D is about skills, 'I learnt cloud systems', which is not about number of jobs.

Both show that foreign hires help locals. A say the projects 'created 150 more jobs, most of them filled by locals' and D say he learnt from 'a colleague from abroad' and now 'lead a team of twelve'. They differ in the type of benefit, A is jobs ('150 more jobs') and D is skills ('I learnt cloud systems'). They also differ in why they say it. A is the boss speaking at a business forum, he need to defend why his firm 'hired 40 engineers from abroad' so he give the nice number. D is just telling a newspaper about his own career, he got nothing to defend.
It is useful because it is written by a local graduate who is looking for a job, so he knows about hiring.

Hiring should be fair to everyone. Companies should hire locals first because this is our country and we served national service. Foreigners are cheaper so the bosses like them. So the source is useful to show that it is unfair.

It is useful because it show that some locals feel they are not given a chance. He sent '60 applications in a year' and at the interview 'the whole team had been brought in from overseas', so he feel the firm prefer foreigners over him.

It is useful because it show that some locals feel they are not given a chance. He sent '60 applications in a year' and at the interview 'the whole team had been brought in from overseas'. But it is limited. It is only one person story, and it dont tell us why the other companies reject him or how many locals have the same problem, so we cannot tell if hiring is unfair in general.

It is useful to show some locals feel shut out, he sent '60 applications in a year' and met a team 'brought in from overseas'. It is limited because it is one person only and he is angry, he want people to pity him. But when I check Source C, the ministry say '300 firms were placed on a watchlist for not giving locals fair consideration'. So what he say is not made up, unfair hiring do happen. So B is useful as a real example of the problem, but not useful to know how common it is.

I disagree. Foreigners take away our jobs and make everything more crowded. My uncle lost his job to a foreigner who was paid less. The government should protect local workers first. So hiring foreign professionals has not benefited local workers.
Source A agrees with the statement and Source D also agrees. Source B disagrees and Source C disagrees. So it is two against two and I agree to a moderate extent.

I disagree with the statement. Source B show a local who sent '60 applications in a year' and still no job, while the whole team was 'brought in from overseas', so locals lose out. Source D agree as he learnt from a foreign colleague and now 'lead a team of twelve'. Source B disagree, he sent '60 applications in a year' and the team was all 'brought in from overseas', so he did not benefit. Thus there are sources that agree and sources that disagree, so I agree to some extent only.

B is only one case but C prove there are such cases. So I agree to a large extent, locals who get in do benefit, but some firms dont let locals in fairly.
Source A tells me the students were sent to a nursing home for six hours and most of them stood at the back and looked at their phones, and the writer signed the form and never went again.

Community service is when students go and help people like the elderly. My school also make us do it. I think it is good because we learn to be grateful. Source A is a student's reflection in a school magazine.
It tells me that compulsory community service does not really make students care, they just do it to get it over with.
It tells me students treat compulsory service as a task to finish and not a way to help. This is shown when the writer says 'We were sent to a nursing home for our six hours'.

compulsory service can become just a task to clear and not real helping. the students 'stood at the back and looked at our phones' and the writer 'signed the form and never went again'. this show they only went there for the hours and the form, they were not there for the old folks at all.
It is reliable because the principal is in charge of the school so he knows his students best.
It is reliable because it says 'every one of our students completes community service', so the students are 'caring and committed to serving others'.
It is not reliable. The principal use very nice words like 'caring and committed' and say 'every one' of the students. It sound too good to be true and he is just praising his own school.

It is not reliable. B say the students are 'caring and committed'. But in Source A the students 'looked at our phones' and the writer 'never went again'. Source C also say school groups 'come once, for the hours'. So A and C both show the students finish the hours but they dont really care, which go against B.

It is not reliable about attitude. B say students are 'caring and committed' but Source A say they 'looked at our phones' and Source C say school groups 'come once, for the hours'. So doing the hours is not the same as caring. Also B is a principal speech to parents at the open house. He want the parents to choose his school, so he make a rule that every student must follow sound like the students have good character.

Source B says my customers buy sofas and cupboards and they cannot carry them to a bus stop and my weekend sales fell by a third. Source C says on car-free Sundays every table is full and families stay for hours because the children can run about on the street.
they are different in what happen to their business. B say 'my weekend sales fell by a third' so he lose money. C say 'every table is full' so the café earn more on car-free days.

C is writing in the neighbourhood newsletter for the neighbours, she want them to come and support the car-free Sundays.
It is useful because it is a notice from the transport agency which is the government, so it is official and it is about the car-free weekends.

Car-free weekends are good for the earth because cars produce carbon dioxide which cause global warming. More towns should do this and people should cycle more. So the source is useful to show we must protect the environment.
It is useful as it tell us more people came to the town centre during the trial. It say 'footfall rose 30%' so the street was more crowded and lively when the cars were not there.

It is useful as it tell us more people came to the town centre, 'footfall rose 30%'. However it is limited. It only give one number for the whole street. It dont say which shops did better or worse, or how people who cannot walk far get there.

In Source B the furniture shop 'weekend sales fell by a third' and in Source D the drop-off point is '300 metres from the clinic'. A never mention these. This is because A is the agency own notice to announce the scheme is permanent, so it only report the result that support its decision. So A is useful for the crowd overall but not for the effect on every shop and resident.

I agree. With no cars the air is fresher and it is safer for children. I went to a car-free street before and it was very fun, there were buskers and food stalls. People should walk more anyway. So car-free weekends improve the town centre.
Source A and Source C agree that car-free weekends improved the town centre. Source B and Source D do not agree. Since there are two sources each side, I agree to half extent.

I agree. Source A say 'footfall rose 30% and air quality improved', so more people come and the air is cleaner. Source C also agree because 'every table is full' and families stay for hours, so the shops are busier and people enjoy the street.

On the other hand Source B disagree as his 'weekend sales fell by a third', so his shop is worse off. Source D disagree, the drop-off is now '300 metres from the clinic' which is far for her. Hence there are good and bad points and I agree to some extent.

Source D disagree, the drop-off is '300 metres from the clinic'. A is the agency defending its own scheme, but C the café is full which match the footfall number, so I believe the gain is real. B and D only speak for themself, but A and C never answer their problem. So I agree to a large extent, most people get a livelier and cleaner centre, but shops selling big things and people who cannot walk far are worse off.
Source C tells me that after the message went round her neighbour of ten years stopped greeting her in the lift, and it took weeks before she spoke to her again.

It is not reliable. A say 'a group of foreigners' was damaging cars. But Source B the police statement say a '15-year-old resident has been arrested' and 'no group was involved'. So the police show A is wrong about who did it, only the part about cars being damage is true.

It is not reliable. A say 'a group of foreigners' damage the cars but Source B say a '15-year-old resident has been arrested' and 'no group was involved', so only the damage is true. Also nobody know who send A, and it tell readers 'Forward to everyone'. So it is written to make residents scared and to spread quickly, not to report what really happen, thats why it blame a group with no proof.
